panels.title: Producer vs Consumer rate
panels.description: Net = consumer - producer. Rates clamped at 100k/s to drop re-seed/restart rate() artifacts.

panels.title: ETA until caught up
panels.description: lag / net-drain, net-drain = -d(lag)/dt over 10m (smoothed). Unreliable for ~10m after a re-seed (the offset rewind distorts the slope); a huge value means net drain <= 0 (not catching up).

panels.title: ETA until caught up (trend)
panels.description: lag / net-drain, net-drain = -d(lag)/dt over 10m (smoothed). Unreliable for ~10m after a re-seed (the offset rewind distorts the slope); a huge value means net drain <= 0 (not catching up). Trending down = converging; flat/rising = falling behind.

panels.title: Change type by embedding impact
panels.description: Per-article: changed=an embedding-input field (name/desc/manufacturer/category/ean/mfr-no/type) actually changed → re-embed (GPU cost); unchanged=vectors reused; new=first index; model-bump=embedding model changed.

panels.title: Embedding-input change ratio
panels.description: Fraction of processed articles touching embedding inputs — the share of the change stream that hits TEI/GPU.

panels.title: Buffer vendor fan-out (vendors / buffer)
panels.description: Distinct vendors per fetched buffer = number of per-vendor $in query waves (each wave capped at MAX_CONCURRENT_QUERIES=8). High p95/p99 marks the slow Mongo-fetch stretches.

panels.title: Avg latency per stage
panels.description: Highest line = current bottleneck. mongo_fetch is backpressure-inflated (wraps downstream).
